description: Inflammation of the udder, usually caused by bacteria entering through the teat canal during milking or in unhygienic housing. Common in dairy cattle and buffalo; ranges from mild subclinical cases to severe toxic mastitis requiring urgent treatment.
symptoms: abnormal milk with clots or flakes
first_aid: Strip out affected quarters gently and discard abnormal milk safely; do not feed it to calves.
Apply a clean cold compress to a hot swollen quarter for short periods if the animal allows.
Ensure clean, dry bedding and milk only with washed hands and clean equipment.
Withhold milk from the food chain until a veterinarian advises it is safe.
Call a veterinarian promptly for antibiotics and pain management; severe cases can become systemic quickly.
